title: PCE price index excluding energy goods
gist: FRED now publishes a PCE price index excluding only energy goods, an underlying-inflation gauge that removes ~2.6% of expenditures (vs ~12% for core PCE since 2012) while being substantially less volatile than headline PCE.

themes.theme: PCE excluding energy goods as inflation gauge

insights.claim: The St. Louis Fed's FRED database now publishes a PCE price index excluding energy goods, available monthly back to January 1959, as an alternative measure of underlying inflation.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: New series to track alongside core PCE for Fed reaction-function analysis.

insights.claim: Core PCE inflation, which excludes food, energy goods and energy services, removes about 12% of consumption expenditures on average since 2012, whereas PCE excluding only energy goods removes about 2.6%.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Core PCE discards a large chunk of the basket (incl. food), so it can diverge from the inflation households experience.
insights.quote: by excluding food, energy goods, and energy services, core inflation removes a substantial share of consumption expenditures. About 12% on average since 2012.
insights.locator: Headline measures such as this one

insights.claim: PCE inflation excluding only energy goods preserves much of the smoothness of core PCE while staying more representative of total consumption, making it substantially less volatile than headline PCE while tracking its broad trends.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: If this gauge gains traction at the Fed, food inflation would matter more for policy than under core PCE.

insights.claim: The Federal Reserve has explicitly targeted 2% inflation since January 2012, measured as the 12-month change in the headline personal consumption expenditures price index.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: The official target is headline, not core — underlying gauges guide but don't replace it.
